title: Noah's Ark IQ
subtitle: One boat, two of every kind, forty days of rain.

questions.text: Why did God decide to send the flood?

options.text: The earth was full of violence and wickedness
options.explanation: Genesis 6:11-13 says the earth was corrupt and filled with violence, so God determined to end it.

options.text: The people had built a great tower
options.explanation: The tower of Babel came after the flood, not before it.

options.text: A famine had ruined the land
options.explanation: There was no famine here. The flood came because of the earth's wickedness.

options.text: The people refused to pay tribute
options.explanation: Tribute had nothing to do with it. The cause was widespread evil.

questions.text: What material was Noah told to build the ark from?

options.explanation: Cedar was used for later buildings like the temple, but the ark used a different wood.
Genesis 6:14 says, "Make thee an ark of gopher wood" (ASV).
Acacia wood was used for the ark of the covenant, not Noah's ark.
Olive trees gave the dove its leaf, but the ark was made of gopher wood.

questions.text: How many people were saved on the ark?

options.explanation: Two was the number for many animals, not for the people aboard.
Close, but the count of people was higher than four.
Noah, his wife, his three sons, and their wives made eight. 1 Peter 3:20 confirms eight souls were saved.
Twelve points to the tribes of Israel, not the family on the ark.

questions.text: What were the names of Noah's three sons?

options.explanation: Those were sons of Adam and Eve, generations before Noah.
Genesis 6:10 names Noah's three sons as Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
Those names belong to the family of Abraham, much later in Genesis.
Those were sons of Jacob, not sons of Noah.

questions.text: How many of each kind of clean animal did Noah bring onto the ark?

options.explanation: Two was the rule for the unclean animals. Clean animals had a larger number.
Genesis 7:2 tells Noah to take clean beasts by sevens, the male and his female.
The number for clean animals was seven, not ten.
One animal could not continue its kind. Clean animals came by sevens.

questions.text: How many days and nights did the rain fall?

options.explanation: Seven days passed before the rain began, but the rain itself lasted longer.
Genesis 7:12 says the rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.
The waters stayed high for a hundred and fifty days, but the rain fell for forty.
That number is too high. The rain lasted forty days and nights.

questions.text: Where did the ark come to rest when the waters went down?

options.explanation: Genesis 8:4 says the ark rested upon the mountains of Ararat.
Mount Sinai is where Moses received the Law, not where the ark landed.
Mount Nebo is where Moses viewed the promised land, far from the ark's resting place.
Bethel was a later worship site. The ark rested on the mountains of Ararat.

questions.text: Which bird did Noah send out first to check if the waters had gone down?

options.explanation: The dove came later. Noah sent out a different bird first.
Genesis 8:7 says Noah sent forth a raven, which went to and fro until the waters were dried up.
No eagle was sent. The first bird out was a raven.
There was no sparrow in this account. Noah first sent a raven.

questions.text: What did the dove bring back that showed the waters had gone down?

options.explanation: The dove did not bring a fish. It returned with a sign from the land.
Genesis 8:11 says the dove came back with an olive leaf plucked off, so Noah knew the waters had abated.
It was not wheat. The dove returned with a fresh olive leaf in its beak.
A stone would prove nothing. The dove brought back an olive leaf.

questions.text: What did Noah do first after he came out of the ark?

options.explanation: Noah did plant a vineyard, but that came a little later, not first.

options.text: He built an altar and offered sacrifices
options.explanation: Genesis 8:20 says Noah built an altar unto the LORD and offered burnt offerings on it.
Noah did not build a city. His first act was to build an altar and worship.

options.text: He set out to find other survivors
options.explanation: There were no other survivors to find. Noah's first act was to build an altar.

questions.text: What sign did God give as the token of His covenant never to flood the whole earth again?

options.explanation: Genesis 9:13 says, "I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant" (ASV).
A star marked other moments in Scripture, but the flood covenant sign was the rainbow.
The pillar of cloud guided Israel in the Exodus. The covenant sign here was the rainbow.
The burning bush was Moses' encounter with God, not the sign of the flood covenant.

questions.text: How old did Noah live to be?

options.explanation: Noah was 600 when the flood came, but he lived much longer after that.
Close, but the text gives a higher total for his full life.
Genesis 9:29 says all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years, and he died.
The number 120 appears in Genesis 6:3 as a limit on human days, but Noah himself lived to 950.
